classification.difficultyReason: Unpack composition to distinguish changing the input in f(h(x)) from changing the output in k(P(x)), then apply the corresponding translation to landmarks on each supplied graph.

content.prompt: The composition of functions can sometimes result in translations.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Consider $y=f(x)$ below.

Let $h(x)=x-3$.

Sketch $f(h(x))$ on the same set of axes.

spec.description: Base curve recovered by translating the printed f(x-3) answer curve three units left. Original labelled features (0,3),(1,4),(2,3),(3,0), with left approach to y=1.
spec.mathematics: Every coordinate and Bézier control point is the source answer coordinate minus (3,0).
spec.sourceCorrection: The source prints the translated answer curve but omits a distinct original curve despite referring to it in the task. Recover the uniquely determined original through the inverse translation; preserve the printed answer as answer-only content.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(h(x))&=f(x-3)\end{align*}$$
Replacing $x$ with $x-3$ translates the graph 3 units right. Each point $(x,y)$ moves to $(x+3,y)$.

spec.description: Qualitative answer curve with leftward approach to height 1, guide intersections (3,3) and (5,3), maximum (4,4), x-intercept 6 and downward right continuation. Bézier segments describe the supplied qualitative features, not an inferred function equation.
spec.mathematics: Graph of y=f(x-3), obtained by translating y=f(x) 3 units right.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer only; the original graph is not distinguishable in the supplied source.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Consider $P(x)$ below.

Let $k(x)=x+2$.

Sketch $k(P(x))$ on the same set of axes.

spec.description: Base curve recovered by translating the printed P(x)+2 answer curve two units down. Original points (-1,0),(0,1),(2,0),(3,1).
spec.mathematics: Every coordinate and Bézier control point is the source answer coordinate minus (0,2).
spec.sourceCorrection: The source prints the translated answer curve but omits a distinct original curve despite referring to it in the task. Recover the uniquely determined original through the inverse translation; preserve the printed answer as answer-only content.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}k(P(x))&=P(x)+2\\y-2&=P(x)\end{align*}$$
Replacing $y$ with $y-2$ translates the graph 2 units up. Each point $(x,y)$ moves to $(x,y+2)$.

spec.description: Qualitative cubic-like answer curve through (-1,2), local maximum (0,3), local minimum (2,2) and (3,3), with downward left and upward right continuation. Bézier segments preserve labelled features without assigning an unsupported polynomial.
spec.mathematics: Graph of y=P(x)+2, obtained by translating P(x) 2 units up.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer only; the original graph is not distinguishable in the supplied source.
